parse.title: Increased introspection
parse.wikitext:
<onlyinclude>
'''Increased introspection''' is a [[learning techniques|metacognitive]] effect defined as the state of mind in which a person feels encouraged to reflect upon and examine their internal psychological processes, judgements, or perceptions.<ref>{{Citation | title=APA Dictionary of Psychology | url=https://dictionary.apa.org/introspection | access-date=15 October 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite book | vauthors=((Schwitzgebel, E.)) | veditors=((Zalta, E. N.)) | date= 2019 | chapter=The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy | title=Introspection | publisher=Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University | edition=Winter 2019 | url=https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/win2019/entries/introspection/}}</ref><ref name="Palhano-Fontes2015">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Palhano-Fontes, F.)), ((Andrade, K. C.)), ((Tofoli, L. F.)), ((Santos, A. C.)), ((Crippa, J. A. S.)), ((Hallak, J. E. C.)), ((Ribeiro, S.)), ((Araujo, D. B. de)) | veditors=((Hu, D.)) | journal=PLOS ONE | title=The Psychedelic State Induced by Ayahuasca Modulates the Activity and Connectivity of the Default Mode Network | volume=10 | issue=2 | pages=e0118143 | date=18 February 2015 | url=https://dx.plos.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0118143 | issn=1932-6203 | doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0118143 | access-date=19 October 2022}}</ref><ref name="Frank2019">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Frank, P.)), ((Sundermann, A.)), ((Fischer, D.)) | journal=International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education | title=How mindfulness training cultivates introspection and competence development for sustainable consumption | volume=20 | issue=6 | pages=1002–1021 | date=4 October 2019 | url=https://www.emerald.com/insight/content/doi/10.1108/IJSHE-12-2018-0239/full/html | issn=1467-6370 | doi=10.1108/IJSHE-12-2018-0239 | access-date=19 October 2022}}</ref><ref name="Fox2012">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Fox, K. C. R.)), ((Zakarauskas, P.)), ((Dixon, M.)), ((Ellamil, M.)), ((Thompson, E.)), ((Christoff, K.)) | veditors=((Martinez, L. M.)) | journal=PLoS ONE | title=Meditation Experience Predicts Introspective Accuracy | volume=7 | issue=9 | pages=e45370 | date=25 September 2012 | url=https://dx.plos.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0045370 | issn=1932-6203 | doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0045370 | access-date=20 October 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Overgaard, M.)), ((Mogensen, J.)) | journal=Review of Philosophy and Psychology | title=An integrative view on consciousness and introspection | volume=8 | issue=1 | pages=129–141 | date= March 2017 | url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s13164-016-0303-6 | issn=1878-5158 | doi=10.1007/s13164-016-0303-6 | access-date=20 October 2022}}</ref> Questions such as "Why am I feeling so?", "How can I describe it?", "How may I cease/sustain this undesirable/desirable experience?" are examples of introspection.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Xue, H.)), ((Desmet, P. M. A.)) | journal=Design Studies | title=Researcher introspection for experience-driven design research | volume=63 | pages=37–64 | date= July 2019 | url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0142694X19300158 | issn=0142694X | doi=10.1016/j.destud.2019.03.001 | access-date=20 October 2022}}</ref> It is important to note that introspection is only an inner observation; verbalizing the contents, especially outloud, is considered an entirely different process.<ref>
{{cite journal | vauthors=((Ericsson, K. A.)), ((Fox, M. C.)) | journal=Psychological Bulletin | title=Thinking aloud is not a form of introspection but a qualitatively different methodology: Reply to Schooler (2011). | volume=137 | issue=2 | pages=351–354 | date= 2011 | url=http://doi.apa.org/getdoi.cfm?doi=10.1037/a0022388 | issn=1939-1455 | doi=10.1037/a0022388 | access-date=20 October 2022}}</ref>

This state of mind is effective at facilitating therapeutic self-improvement and positive personal growth. Contrary to early psychological assumptions, introspection appears to be an ability that can be honed; humans do not have automatic or unbiased access to experience.<ref name="Frank2019" /><ref name="Fox2012" /> Increasing introspection often results in insightful resolutions to the present situation, future possibilities, insecurities, and goals coinciding with personal acceptance of insecurities, fears, hopes, struggles, and traumas. 

Increased introspection is likely the result of a combination of an appropriate setting in conjunction with other coinciding effects such as [[analysis enhancement]], [[mindfulness]],<ref name="Frank2019" /> and [[personal bias suppression]]. It is most commonly induced during [[meditation]]<ref name="Fox2012" /> or under the influence of [[dosage#common|moderate]] [[dosage|dosages]] of [[hallucinogen|hallucinogenic]] compounds, such as [[psychedelic|psychedelics]]<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Riga, M. S.)), ((Soria, G.)), ((Tudela, R.)), ((Artigas, F.)), ((Celada, P.)) | journal=The International Journal of Neuropsychopharmacology | title=The natural hallucinogen 5-MeO-DMT, component of Ayahuasca, disrupts cortical function in rats: reversal by antipsychotic drugs | volume=17 | issue=08 | pages=1269–1282 | date= August 2014 | url=https://academic.oup.com/ijnp/article-lookup/doi/10.1017/S1461145714000261 | issn=1461-1457 | doi=10.1017/S1461145714000261 | access-date=19 October 2022}}</ref> and [[dissociative|dissociatives]].<ref name="Palhano-Fontes2015" /><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Barker, S. A.)) | journal=Frontiers in Neuroscience | title=N, N-Dimethyltryptamine (DMT), an Endogenous Hallucinogen: Past, Present, and Future Research to Determine Its Role and Function | volume=12 | pages=536 | date=6 August 2018 | url=https://www.frontiersin.org/article/10.3389/fnins.2018.00536/full | issn=1662-453X | doi=10.3389/fnins.2018.00536 | access-date=19 October 2022}}</ref><ref>
{{cite journal | vauthors=((Santos, R. G. dos)), ((Osório, F. L.)), ((Crippa, J. A. S.)), ((Hallak, J. E. C.)) | journal=Neuroscience & Biobehavioral Reviews | title=Classical hallucinogens and neuroimaging: A systematic review of human studies | volume=71 | pages=715–728 | date= December 2016 | url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0149763416302354 | issn=01497634 | doi=10.1016/j.neubiorev.2016.10.026 | access-date=19 October 2022}}</ref> However, it can also occur in a less consistent form under the influence of [[entactogens]].
</onlyinclude>

===Relational Embeddedness===
Relational embeddedness is defined as a remarkable insight or transformation involving a significant personal relationship.<ref name="BelserAgin-Liebes2017">{{cite journal|last1=Belser|first1=Alexander B.|last2=Agin-Liebes|first2=Gabrielle|last3=Swift|first3=T. Cody|last4=Terrana|first4=Sara|last5=Devenot|first5=Neşe|last6=Friedman|first6=Harris L.|last7=Guss|first7=Jeffrey|last8=Bossis|first8=Anthony|last9=Ross|first9=Stephen|title=Patient Experiences of Psilocybin-Assisted Psychotherapy: An Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis|journal=Journal of Humanistic Psychology|volume=57|issue=4|year=2017|pages=354–388|issn=0022-1678|doi=10.1177/0022167817706884}}</ref> A small sample size of [[psilocybin]] therapy patients unanimously addressed crucial aspects of their personal relationship histories without interviewer prompting. These insights are most likely to be about immediate family members or loved ones.

This experienced is marked by radical acceptance and forgiveness for the focused loved one along with a [[catharsis]]. Occasionally participants describe loved ones appearing as [[autonomous entities|spirits]] sent to guide them.
